is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated field-collected Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii from Kpomè, Southern Benin (p. 3-4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The authors only performed molecular speciation for species identification (An. funestus s.s. and An. coluzzii). No target insecticide resistance markers (e.g., Vgsc kdr, Ace-1, GSTe2, Cyp6p9a/b) were genotyped in this paper.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts, allele counts, or allele frequencies for target resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as adults (An. funestus) or larvae (An. coluzzii) in Kpomè, Southern Benin in June 2017 (p. 3-4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study conducting bioassays, cone tests, tunnel tests, HPLC net analyses, and experimental hut trials in Benin.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study site is Kpomè, Southern Benin (coordinates: 6° 23' N, 2° 13' E) (p. 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field collection of mosquitoes took place in June 2017 and experimental hut trials were conducted in August 2017 (p. 3, 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine field collection and experimental hut trial conducted in Kpomè in 2017.

supplement.evidence: No target marker genotyping was conducted; no missing data in supplements required for marker analysis.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy of pyrethroid and pyrethroid-PBO treated nets against field-collected multi-resistant Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii populations from Kpomè, Southern Benin, using WHO cone tests, tunnel tests, and experimental hut release-recapture trials. No target insecticide resistance markers were genotyped.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report target resistance markers or extractable genotype data (only molecular speciation and bioassays were performed).
